A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 24-page versions of the same study. The main text, figures, tables, mathematical definitions, and Appendices A and B can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and the appendices report original evaluations on 104 Mind2Web-Live tasks, including planning, execution, replanning, model comparisons, and manual validation of LLM judges.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main experiments, additional model results in Appendix B.4, and judge-validation outcomes in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The NL/PDDL planning procedures, low-level execution, LLM postcondition checking, and replanning mechanism are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same operational prompts apart from a quotation-mark correction.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Mind2Web-Live web-task coverage. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed; the new data-release statement concerns access rather than experimental coverage.

E2.justification: The human/NL/PDDL plan comparisons, action-representation comparisons, and evaluated models remain the same: gpt-5-nano, claude-haiku-4.5, and gemini-flash-2.5. Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding main-text and appendix experiments.

E3.justification: Both retain the 104-task test set, text-based DOM observations, action settings, gpt-5-nano judging, evaluation metrics, and single replanning round. The 50-example judge-validation checks in Appendix A.3 are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The decomposition/executability analysis, action-space comparisons, replanning analyses, failure examples, and judge-validation study are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains unchanged. Both present point estimates without reporting repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains 60.6% NL and 67.7% PDDL perfect-match rates, while Appendix A.3 retains 82% and 86% judge agreement.

T1.justification: The definitions of plans, trajectories, postcondition checking, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core claims: hierarchical evaluation diagnoses failures, PDDL supports more concise planning, execution is the main bottleneck, and replanning improves outcomes.

C2.justification: The explanations of planning and execution failures and the design recommendations are unchanged. Limitations still cover restricted configurations, absent multimodal evaluation, and dependence on annotated reference plans.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future framework release; v2 states that the framework and data are released and supplies a repository link in footnote 1. Existing implementation descriptions and appendix prompts are otherwise unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the repository's contents.

R1.justification: Section 7 and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning, including the novelty claim about incorporating formal planning representations into web agents.

P1.justification: v2 revises the release sentence, adds a short funding-acknowledgments section, and corrects an appendix quotation mark. The scientific narrative and main section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added footnote and acknowledgments cause text reflow. Table 4 changes columns, Table 5 moves from PDF page 6 to page 7, and printed page numbers disappear. Figure and table contents, structures, and numbering are retained.

improvement.justification: The repository pointer and explicit framework-and-data release statement modestly improve access and reproducibility documentation over v1's unlinked future promise. Scientific evidence and conclusions are unchanged. This is a documentation gain; the supplied PDFs cannot verify repository availability or completeness.
